mmlu.name: MMLU
mmlu.desc: Fifty-seven subjects of multiple-choice questions, from elementary mathematics to law and medicine, written to test what a model knows rather than what it can reason through. For three years it was the default number on every model card.

gsm8k.name: GSM8K
gsm8k.desc: About 8,500 grade-school math word problems that take two to eight steps to solve. In 2021 the best models got a fifth of them right; by 2024 it was effectively finished and stopped being reported.

math5.name: MATH (level 5)
math5.desc: Competition problems from AMC and AIME-style contests, graded by difficulty; level 5 is the hardest tier. The 2021 paper predicted these would stay out of reach for years.

gpqa.name: GPQA Diamond
gpqa.desc: 198 graduate-level questions in biology, physics and chemistry written by PhDs and checked to be "Google-proof": experts outside the field with unlimited web access scored about 34 percent. The Diamond subset is the cleanest tier.

aime.name: AIME (OTIS mock)
aime.desc: The American Invitational Mathematics Examination is the qualifier for the U.S. olympiad team. Epoch runs models on a set of mock AIME problems written for the OTIS training program, so the questions are new to the models.

swe.name: SWE-bench Verified
swe.desc: Five hundred real GitHub issues from open-source Python projects, each one checked by a human to be solvable. A model has to read the repository, write the fix and pass the project's own tests. The closest thing to a work sample for software engineering.

arcagi.name: ARC-AGI
arcagi.desc: Abstract visual puzzles designed by François Chollet in 2019 to resist memorization: each task shows a few examples of a transformation and asks for the rule. Trivial for people, and unsolved by AI for five years.

arcagi2.name: ARC-AGI-2
arcagi2.desc: The 2025 successor, rebuilt after the first version fell, with tasks that require composing several rules at once. Every task was verified solvable by at least two people.

hle.name: Humanity's Last Exam
hle.desc: About 2,500 questions from nearly a thousand subject experts across more than a hundred fields, built by the Center for AI Safety and Scale AI specifically because earlier benchmarks had saturated. The official leaderboard runs the full exam including images; text-only subsets score higher.

fm13.name: FrontierMath (tiers 1–3)
fm13.desc: Unpublished research-level mathematics problems written by mathematicians and kept private so they cannot leak into training data. Tiers 1 to 3 range from advanced undergraduate to early research; a fourth tier is harder still.

metr.name: METR time horizon
metr.desc: Rather than a score, METR measures the length of software task, in human-minutes, that a model completes successfully half the time. It is the one measure here with no ceiling, and it has been doubling every few months.
